observations: body L1-L4: «Abrāhām bar Ḥiyyā» and «al–Battānī» (L3) are letter-spaced; the long dashes of «Hebraeo–Hispanus», «al–Battānī» and «al–Ma’mūn» measure 5.3, 5.4 and 5.3 pt. Al-Battānī observed at ar-Raqqah from 877 to 918 and died in 929; al-Ma’mūn reigned from 813 to 833, whence the «sic!».

body L7-L16: the table is set with each piece placed as printed: the whole numbers on their right edges, the fractions and note numbers from their left edges. Ibn Rosteh gives no least distance of the Moon; the print sets five dots there. The dash of «Al–Farghānī» measures 4.2 pt. The numbers of the notes check: 33 ½ 1/20 radii of 3250 miles are 109037 ½ miles (note 2), 64 ⅙ radii of 3818 miles are 244988 ⅓ (note 3), and 8820 radii of 3818 miles are 33674760 (note 5). Bar Ḥiyyā's 1146, 8000, 12400 and 18000 follow al-Battānī's 1146, 8022, 12924 and 18094 (translation, p. 121, l. 30-31, and p. 122, l. 12 and 24), as notes 6, 8 and 9 say.

body L7-L16: Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXV-LXXVI) find Ibn Rosteh's numbers in Thābit ibn Qurrah's booklet on what is needed before reading the Almagest, extant only in an unpublished Latin version (Venice, codices A and B): least distances Moon 33 Earth radii, Mercury 64, Venus 167, Sun 1079, Mars 1260, Jupiter 8820, Saturn 14187, the greatest of Saturn and the least of the fixed stars 17865 (for Ibn Rosteh's 19880 and 20000); the sizes Sun 166 Earths, stars of the first magnitude 94, Saturn and Jupiter «about» 79, Mars «about» 1 ½, Venus «about» 1/87, Moon 1/40 (A 1/10), Mercury 1/29680 (A 1/29683). The agreement is in the Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn; Thābit's 64 and 167 for Mercury and Venus differ from Ibn Rosteh's 64 ⅙ and 166 in the table. Another booklet ascribed to Thābit in codex B, «de quantitatibus stellarum», which names al-Farghānī and Ǵābir ibn Aflaḥ, Nallino judges spurious.

body L18-L19, L23-L28: «Ptolemaeo», «al–Qazwīnī» (L18), «Ptolemaeus», «Ptolemaei» and «al–Bīrūnī» are letter-spaced; «al–Qazwīnī» (L26) is not. The long dashes of «al–Qazwīnī», «ad–Damīrī», «II–IX», «al–Qazwīnī», «al–Bīrūnī», «234–36» and «68–» measure 5.3, 5.4, 5.4, 5.5, 5.3, 5.3 and 5.2 pt. The year 161 of the Hiǵrah began on 8 October 777 by the astronomical epoch of the tabular calendar (9 October by the civil epoch).
body L29, L31: «Ya‘qūb ibn Ṭāriq» and «Ya‘qūb» are letter-spaced.

body L19-L22: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXV; AB01-PDF0442-body-L019 to L022): the passage of al-Qazwīnī stands in Wüstenfeld's edition, t. I, p. 18, with the same readings; but after المقالة الثانية the word عشرة has surely fallen out, for not the second but the twelfth book of Euclid is meant, whose 18th proposition says that spheres are to one another in the triplicate ratio of their diameters, the theorem on which the computations chiefly rest. The printed «secundum librum Euclidis» is kept.
notes_left L1-L7: «Abrahamo Hispano filio R. Haijae» is letter-spaced; «190-92» has a hyphen (3.2 pt), and the dash before «Quantitates» measures 8.5 pt.
notes_left L9-L11: the 0 of «109037» prints broken, like a closing parenthesis; 33 ½ 1/20 times 3250 is 109037 ½. Golius' 33 ½ ⅕ is 33.7.
notes_left L12-L13: the Arabic is «ونصف» ‘and a half’, for which read («l.», lege) «ونصف ثلث» ‘and half a third’, that is ⅙: the text has 64 ½ for 64 ⅙. The join of the lam of «ثلث» prints broken.

notes_right L1-L8: «Al-Battānī» is letter-spaced; its hyphen measures 3.2, 3.2 and 3.1 pt in notes 4, 6 and 8, and 4.2 pt in note 9, where it is set as a long dash. The rule between the two columns of the notes prints broken.
notes_right L12-L13: «Sūrya-» and «-Siddhānta» have hyphens (2.5 and 3.4 pt), and so has «84-90» (3.5 pt); «Burgess» and «Whit-» are letter-spaced. The note continues on p. 288.
